clue.text: Deadlock from an unresolved sit-in?

parts.note: a protest sit-in that never ends leaves protesters standing firm and police facing them, a stalemate in which neither side gives way

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a cryptic definition: a sit-in nobody resolves becomes a confrontation where both parties hold their ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-off is a stalemate between opposing parties, exactly what a deadlock is.

clue.text: A month with the Camerons' division

definitions.meaning: The usual short form of September
a branch or subdivision of a Scottish or Irish clan, such as Clan Cameron

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the abbreviation of September and the term for a branch of a clan.

clue.text: Prophet with a reduced majority

indicators.note: reduced tells us to shorten the word for majority by cutting its final letter

parts.note: the majority of something is most of it

explanation.surface: A minor prophet scrapes back into office with fewer votes than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majority' looks political, as a winning margin, but here it simply means most of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament, with a book named after him.

clue.text: Works of Bramante and Brunelleschi, a twosome detailing some with elevation

parts.note: a duo is a pair or twosome

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevation lifts the letters so they read upwards, from bottom to top
de-tailing: the word some loses its tail, its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before its tail is cut

explanation.surface: Two Renaissance architects' buildings are described in lofty detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailing' is split as de-tailing, removing a tail; 'with elevation' works only because this is a down entry, where reading upwards turns letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian cathedrals are called duomos; Brunelleschi built Florence's dome and Bramante designed for St Peter's.

clue.text: Cod alternative from conservationists' fresh find; I'm OK battered!

indicators.note: battered means beaten about, so the letters of these four words are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the letters I and M

explanation.surface: Environmentalists find a fresh fish to replace cod, and it is served battered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' rearranges FRESH FIND I'M OK; 'from conservationists'' links, since they urge a switch away from overfished cod. 'battered' sounds like chip-shop cooking, apt for a fried fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkfish, fried, is a dish recommended as a sustainable substitute for cod.

clue.text: See 26
Make much of dodgy last character with no blame attached

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound or shifty, so these letters are shuffled into a new arrangement

parts.note: Z is the last character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone escapes blame for a shady final role and makes a big deal of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges Z, NO and BLAME; 'attached' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To emblazon is to proclaim or celebrate something conspicuously, making much of it.

clue.text: Deadly poison present! It's all around us!

indicators.note: deadly here is read as wrecking the word that follows, an instruction to rearrange its letters

parts.note: being present means being here

explanation.surface: A warning cry that lethal poison is everywhere about us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deadly' looks like part of a phrase 'deadly poison', but it is the anagram signal acting on the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: This upper layer of the atmosphere surrounds the whole planet, so it is literally all around us.

clue.text: Like an unpaid quarryman on the rocks?

definitions.text: Like an unpaid quarryman on the rocks?

parts.words: Like an unpaid quarryman on the rocks?
parts.note: on the rocks means broke, and a quarryman works with stone, so an unpaid one is penniless in a stony way

explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic definition: the idiom for penniless is read literally for a stone worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Being completely without money is the slang sense, apt for someone whose wages have not been paid.

clue.text: He scored from penetrating for the Ukrainian side

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: penetrating means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Kiev, as in the football club Dynamo Kiev
of can mean from, as in 'a man of Kent'

explanation.surface: A footballer scores after breaking through the Ukrainian team's defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' suggests a goal, keeping up the football picture, but it means composed music; Kiev stands for its football club, Dynamo Kiev.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian composer wrote film and ballet scores, so he is one who scored music.

clue.text: Died in vain, sadly; can Edwina produce from 21?

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for died inside the rearranged word
sadly signals the word vain is in a bad way, its letters jumbled

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died in records and genealogies
can is slang for a lavatory, a loo
Edwina Currie, a British Conservative politician, whose surname sounds just like the dish

explanation.surface: A complaint about someone who died for nothing, and whether a politician can make something of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges VAIN to VINA and 'in' puts D inside to make VINDA. Edwina Currie (the egg-salmonella minister) gives the surname spelt as the dish. 21 is Hell's Kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiery dish suits a kitchen called Hell's, so it is fitting produce from there.

clue.text: House call

definitions.meaning: house is another name for the numbers game played in halls
the shout a winning player gives on completing a card

explanation.definitionFit: The game was long called house, and its name is also what the winner calls out.

clue.text: Gay Scot, a MacDonald, swearing in 21!

parts.note: the Gay Gordons is a Scottish dance, so a gay Scot is a Gordon
Ramsay MacDonald was the first Labour prime minister

explanation.surface: A cheerful Scotsman from Clan MacDonald curses in a hellish place.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is Hell's Kitchen, the TV cookery show; the Gay Gordons is a Scottish country dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The foul-mouthed Scottish chef fronted the television show Hell's Kitchen, famous for his swearing there.

clue.text: Dare to telephone the Queen?

parts.note: to bell someone is British slang for to telephone them
a queen is a female cat

explanation.surface: Would you have the nerve to phone the monarch?
explanation.walkthrough: In the fable only a brave mouse would hang a bell on the cat; a queen is a female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: To bell the cat is to take on a risky task for the common good, so to dare.

clue.text: Tory against privileged lives could be fitting

parts.note: con is short for Conservative, a Tory
v is short for versus, against
U stands for upper-class, the privileged set

indicators.note: could be suggests the next word is only potentially itself, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A Conservative opposing the lifestyles of the privileged might be appropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges LIVES into LSIVE. 'fitting' means having fits, not suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Convulsive describes violent spasms, as in having fits, so it is fitting in that sense.

clue.text: Love giving one aching back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for aching in the opposite direction

parts.note: aching means sore

explanation.surface: Romance gives someone a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SORE round; 'giving one' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love stands for love itself.

clue.text: Wrong name on the rota: how many more?

indicators.note: wrong means in error, so these letters come out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone finds their name wrongly put on the duty roster yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges N plus ON THE ROTA.
explanation.definitionFit: The weary exclamation means 'surely not one more', the same as asking how many more are to come.

clue.text: Believing there's no vacancy among the Guardian's owners, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken and the result spelt by its sound

parts.words: no vacancy among the Guardian's owners
parts.note: the Guardian is owned by the Scott Trust, and no vacancy means full, so the trust is full

explanation.surface: Confident that the Guardian's owning board has no seats free.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian newspaper belongs to the Scott Trust, so the phrase is TRUST FULL, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Trustful means trusting and credulous, ready to believe.

clue.text: Coupling of Héloïse and Abelard?

parts.note: the medieval lovers were united in love, yet Abelard was castrated, so their physical union was cut short; the tie that binds sweethearts is a knot

explanation.walkthrough: Abelard was castrated by Héloïse's uncle, so a pun lurks: their coupling was a 'lovers not'.
explanation.definitionFit: A love knot, an interlaced decorative tie, symbolises the union of sweethearts.

clue.text: Drink for adult travelling with Noah

indicators.note: anyone travelling with Noah was inside his vessel, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: Noah built the ark
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up sailing with Noah orders a spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling with' Noah puts A inside ARK.
explanation.definitionFit: Arak is an aniseed spirit of the Middle East, a strong drink.

clue.text: Critic with pronounced opinions on author Anna

definitions.meaning: Brian ..., the outspoken British art critic known for strong views and a plummy accent

explanation.definitionFit: The surname is shared by the art critic Brian and the novelist Anna.

clue.text: New York slums where 5 on 25 are prepared?

definitions.meaning: a notorious tenement district on Manhattan's West Side
devils on horseback, bacon-wrapped prunes, would be cooked in a kitchen run by the devil

explanation.walkthrough: 5 on 25 is DEVILS on HORSEBACK, a savoury of prunes wrapped in bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manhattan district takes its name from its once-squalid slums, and literally a devil's cookhouse.

clue.text: William Brown's cloven foot

indicators.note: cloven means split, so the name is broken in two and only its second part kept

parts.note: split as Will-i-am, the name yields the pieces before and after
B is the abbreviation for brown, as on pencils and in heraldry

explanation.surface: Just William's boy hero shows a devilish split hoof.
explanation.walkthrough: William Brown is the schoolboy hero of the Just William books; the name William can be split as Will-i-am, as the pop musician styles himself.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot of one short then one long syllable.

clue.text: Island state in the Garden of England

indicators.note: in places the state's abbreviation inside the region's

parts.note: Kent, called the Garden of England, lies in the South East, abbreviated SE
KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: A self-governing territory found within Kent's orchards.
explanation.walkthrough: The Garden of England is Kent, a county in England's South East (SE).
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland.

clue.text: Max or daughter leaving scar

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so these letters go out of the name

parts.note: Max Clifford was a British publicist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrity publicist or his daughter walks out, leaving an emotional scar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes OR and D from CLIFFORD. 'scar' is a steep rock face, not a wound mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a steep rocky crag or bluff, a sense common in northern English place names.

clue.text: Switch bet on runner up here

indicators.note: switch tells us to swap the order, so the runner comes before the bet

parts.note: a horse is a runner in a race
to back is to bet on

explanation.surface: A punter changes his wager on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' turns round the order the clue gives, bet on runner; 'up here' is a cryptic pointer to where a rider sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider on horseback is up, sitting aloft on the animal.

clue.text: Loved this! "Led Astray" by Kingsley Amis

indicators.note: astray means gone off course, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A reader loved a novel by Kingsley Amis titled 'Led Astray'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Astray' rearranges LOVED THIS LED. The Booker-winning novel is by Kingsley Amis.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Devils is the 1986 Booker Prize novel written by Kingsley Amis.

clue.text: One of 2 in 22, but only 1 in 3!

definitions.text: One of 2 in 22, but only 1 in 3!

parts.words: One of 2 in 22, but only 1 in 3!
parts.note: a metrical foot from 22 consists of two such units, while the word three is spoken as a single unit

explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic definition: 22 is an iambic foot of two units, while the word 'three' has just one.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of pronunciation; an iambic foot has two of them and the word three only one.
